general election = a nationwide election to choose a new parliament
proportional representation = an electoral system in which seats match the share of votes
manifesto = a public statement of a party's policies before an election
populism = politics that claims to speak for ordinary people against elites
nationalism = a political belief that puts one's nation first, sometimes at others' expense
swing voter = a voter who is not loyal to one party and can decide an election
secret ballot = a vote in which nobody can see how you chose
hung parliament = a parliament in which no party has an overall majority
opposition = the parties not in government, who criticise those in power
minority government = a government that does not have a majority of seats
vote of no confidence = a parliamentary vote to remove the government from office
grassroots = ordinary members of a party or movement, not its leaders
political spectrum = the range of political views from left to right
incumbent = the person or party currently holding office
suffrage = the right to vote in elections
disenfranchised = deprived of the right to vote
opinion poll = a survey of people's views, often on parties or policies
landslide victory = an election win by a very large margin
abstain = to formally decline to vote for or against a motion
electoral fraud = illegal interference with the process of an election
